newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota seeks sales record of 4.97 million vehicles.
newsitem.headline: Toyota seeks sales record of 4.97 million vehicles.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp. said Tuesday it aims to sell a record 4.97 million vehicles around the world in 1997.
That would be 220,000 more than in 1996, and compares with the existing record of 4.87 million vehicles sold in 1990, a company spokesman said.
Of the total, Toyota hopes to sell a record 2.76 million vehicles overseas, up 140,000 from the existing record of 2.62 million in 1996.
Toyota, Japan's biggest carmaker, said in December it hoped for domestic sales of 2.21 million vehicles in 1997, up from 2.13 million in 1996.
Its share of the domestic market fell to 39.1 percent in 1996, the first time it has been below 40 percent since 1982.
The spokesman said it would try to push the figure back up above 40 percent this year.

He also said Toyota will give more than five billion yen ($43.4 million) in bonuses to its employees to mark the company's 60th anniversary on Aug. 28. It had about 70,000 employees as of last September.
